title: 2026-06-05-redwood-june-2026-all-hands
summary: Monthly company all-hands covering product priorities for Q2, Dedicated/Private rollouts, performance metrics, hiring updates, and security/compliance progress. Leadership answered questions and listed next steps including customer POCs and internal hiring priorities.
action_items: Priya - finalize GPU autoscale playbook - due 2026-06-19
Liam - publish public roadmap update doc and link in #product - due 2026-06-12
Miguel - run end-to-end latency benchmark vs previous quarter and share results - due 2026-06-16
Emma - push updated hiring plan and interview rubric to shared drive - due 2026-06-10
next_steps: Leadership to share Q2 goals and OKRs doc
SEs to start outreach on Dedicated pilot invites
Security to finalize SOC 2 gap remediation list and share with CSMs
Schedule product deep-dive for partners team next week
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia: Good morning everyone, welcome to the June all-hands, thanks for joining, were about an hour and 12 minutes today so well try to keep to time. Uh, quick agenda: Q2 priorities, Dedicated/Private updates, performance metrics, hiring, and Q&A.
[00:22] Miguel: Hi all, quick product ops note before we start. We shipped the model catalog improvements last week so you should see per-route telemetry in Console. Theres a known issue where the timeline timestamps sometimes show PST instead of the user timezone, were tracking it.
[00:45] Priya: Awesome. On engineering priorities: three main focuses this sprint -- autoscaling and burst capacity tuning for Dedicated, prefix and KV cache improvements to reduce token recompute, and continued work on quantization pipelines so customers see consistent quality with 4-bit profiles.
[01:10] Liam: To add, product is prioritizing two headline features Q2: 1) rollout controls in Console (canary/A-B + automatic fallback), and 2) a public-facing cost/perf guide for common workloads. The guide should help teams choose hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[01:36] Sofia: On the business side we exceeded our MRR target for the month by 7% - great work — but pipeline for Dedicated pilots needs to accelerate to hit enterprise commitments. Well be sending out targeted invites for the next wave.
[01:52] Emma: Quick hiring update: were green on IC hiring in infra but we still have gaps in solutions engineering and partnered sales. Were updating interview rubrics to reduce time-to-hire; please send feedback.
[02:12] Speaker 1 (from Finance, unclear): Can you comment on price changes for hosted tiers?
[02:18] Sofia: We arent adjusting list pricing; instead were focusing on packaging and committed capacity discounts on Dedicated, also clearer quotas/overage behavior so customers know what to expect.
[02:36] Miguel: On technical metrics: p95 latency across hosted lowered from 420ms to 350ms for common chat paths after the kernel selection tweak; total token throughput improved ~12% due to better batching heuristics. There are still corner cases above 1 second for long context windows - working on sequence length shaping to avoid that.
[03:05] Priya: A note about KV cache - transcription sometimes shows it as "K V cash" in meeting notes, which made me laugh, but performance-wise the KV cache improvements reduce repeated prefix work by up to 45% on sessions with high reuse.
[03:28] Miguel: Also we rolled out a fallback routing policy that prefers cheaper compatible variants when Dedicated capacity is saturated; this preserves availability. Were collecting signals to automate routing thresholds.
[03:45] Sofia: Security update?
[03:48] Emma: Security team finished their internal SOC 2 pre-assessment, we have three medium-priority items (audit log retention, SSO session rotation, and a few separation of duty clarifications). Weve scheduled a remediation sprint with engineering next week. Also were nearly done with the KMS integrations for Private customers; one vendor has a minor HSM compatibility edge-case.
[04:14] Miguel: On Private deployment: last month we completed two on-prem installs with partner integrators; latency targets met but we had to ship a QoS config to stabilize network egress for one customer. Weve documented the workaround.
[04:32] Liam: Customer stories - sandbox pilot with an AI-native startup showed 30% token cost reduction switching to our batching/cache defaults vs their previous infra. SE team will post a short case study in the partner portal.
[04:50] Sofia: Questions from the audience? Please use the Q&A box.
[05:03] Anonymous (Q in chat): Are we changing target regions? APAC ask has increased.
[05:09] Miguel: We are expanding capacity in APAC region with a partner zone in Singapore later this quarter. Its capacity-first (no dedicated yet) to support trials and reduce latency.
[05:22] Priya: Technical deep dive coming for anyone who wants more details on batching params - next Thursday.
[05:30] Speaker 2 (Engineering): Any guidance on model quantization regressions? We had a customer report on hallucination increase after 4-bit conversion.
[05:39] Priya: Thanks, yes - were maintaining a regression harness tied to prompt sets; the quantization pipeline flags regressions and can fallback to an unquantized variant automatically if quality degrades. The Optimize recommendations will include quantization risk scores soon.
[05:58] Miguel: Were also instrumenting more fine-grained evals in Console so customers can see per-prompt quality deltas between variants.
[06:10] Liam: Revenue ops note: the new per-route analytics landed but we need to tune the quotas UI copy. Marketing will help rewrite.
[06:22] Emma: Org health - our eNPS went up 4 points; a few comments on manager training. Were adding a manager workshop week in July.
[06:36] Sofia: Ok lets quickly run through roadmap bullets and then open floor Q&A.
[06:42] Liam: Roadmap bullets: 1) Console rollout controls GA, 2) Dedicated burst autoscale policy v1, 3) Private control plane improvements (audit logs + KMS workflows), 4) Redwood Optimize public beta for batching suggestions, 5) Security: SOC 2 readiness.
[07:05] Speaker 3 (Sales): For Dedicated pilots, what is the expected onboarding time? We need a number to commit to customers.
[07:13] Miguel: Typical onboarding for Dedicated is 4-6 weeks for standard templates; for Private/on-prem its 6-12 weeks depending on networking and KMS HSM approvals. Were working on a checklist to cut that down.
[07:31] Speaker 4 (CSM): Are we shipping any automation to reduce manual handoffs for pilots?
[07:35] Priya: Yes, theres a pilot automation playbook that SEs can use; it adds infra templates, a standard benchmark harness, and a pre-configured KV cache policy. SEs please pull from the repo.
[07:50] Sofia: Quick shout-out to the infra team for improving CI times and to QE for the regression harness.
[07:58] Miguel: I want to call out two technical risks: 1) GPU driver regressions from vendor updates, 2) wider-memory models causing lock contention. Were increasing smoke tests in CI to catch these earlier.
[08:15] Priya: On the memory side were testing split-KV strategies and better kernel selection heuristics to reduce contention.
[08:27] Liam: Product note - were reworking the onboarding flow so Trial customers get a sample prompt set and can run a one-click benchmark. That should reduce initial drop-off.
[08:40] Emma: People update - org chart tweaks: moving platform reliability into infra and promoting two senior engineers to staff. Well post updated org docs after this call.
[08:55] Q&A (various short questions): Some folks asked about parental leave updates, expense policy clarifications, and the All-Hands recording. Emma: well update policy doc and post the recording.
[09:12] Speaker 5 (Marketing): Any guidance on messaging for the next press piece on performance wins?
[09:17] Sofia: Keep it engineering-led, focus on reproducible benchmarks and cost delta stories. Dont oversell the numbers; link to the verification harness. Miguel will share a short data pack.
[09:35] Miguel: Ill share the benchmark spreadsheet in #product and link in the all-hands notes.
[09:45] Priya: Quick technical tangent - were introducing a lightweight kernel selection profiler for realtime tuning; its experimental but could help ops.
[09:58] Sofia: Ok closing remarks: team, incredible work. Focus on hitting the Dedicated pilot targets and close the SOC 2 items. Well do a follow-up leadership sync next week. Thanks.
[10:10] Transcript end.
